text:
jamie_oncall: 🚨 Monitoring alert — sudden 5xx spike on /v1/generate in hosted inference (us-west1). 5xx rate ~15% over last 6m, p50 latency doubled. Canary rollout r-2026-0315-32 moved from 5% -> 20% at ~2143658460. Seen from 10:08 UTC.

deploy-bot: Deploy r-2026-0315-32 applied at 2026-03-15T10:05Z to target pools: [inference-runner-v2, inference-runner-v3-canary]. Feature flags: {"aggressive_batching": true, "kv_cache_invalidate": false}.

ella_infra: quick check — it looks like the canary was mistargeted: some hosts in inference-runner-v2 are still on kernel 0.9 and have 32GB GPU memory. aggressive_batching increases per-request KV/cache growth; combined with kernel mismatch -> OOMs in the runner. Logs show repeated "OOM while allocating attention cache" followed by upstream connection resets.

maya_eng: Confirmed. Runner logs from host xwr-02: 
```
2026-03-15T10:09:12Z ERROR model-runner: OOM allocating attention_cache (requested 1200MB)
2026-03-15T10:09:12Z WARN gateway: upstream reset while streaming token (connection reset by peer)
2026-03-15T10:09:13Z ERROR api: 502 Bad Gateway: upstream unavailable
```

maya_eng: Repro steps locally (fast repro at high batch):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "x-model: openllm-v2" \
  -H "x-deploy-rollout: r-2026-0315-32-canary" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"prompt":"long prompt...","max_tokens":1024,"batch_size":16}'
# returns 502 consistently when batch_size > 8 on v2 hosts
```

tariq_support: Customer reports: acme-inc called at 10:15 UTC about repeated 502s. No billing issues yet, but UX is broken. They provided request id: req_0a1b2c3d.

kevin_sre: Agreed we should stop rollout + rollback flag. Immediate mitigation: set canary percent -> 0 and disable aggressive batching on canary targets. I'll run rollback.

kevin_sre: PATCH /admin/rollouts/r-2026-0315-32 
```
{ "canary_percent": 0 }
```

kevin_sre: Also disabling the feature flag for that rollout: 
```
POST /admin/flags/patch {"flag":"aggressive_batching","target":"r-2026-0315-32","value":false}
```

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by @kevin_sre at 2026-03-15T10:24:05Z. Traffic shifting to 0% canary. Expected convergence ~30s.

jamie_oncall: Telemetry update: by 10:27 UTC 5xx rate dropping, by 10:29 back to baseline. p50/p95 latency normalized. No more OOMs observed on v2 hosts.

maya_eng: Root cause summary: rollout targeted a mixed-capability pool (v2 with older kernel + smaller memory) while enabling aggressive_batching. That combination increased per-request memory pressure, causing model-runner OOMs -> upstream resets -> gateway 5xx.

tariq_support: Customer update drafted — apology + explain rollback + offer pro-rated credits if they saw errors longer than 5m. Will send after postmortem.

ella_infra: Action items: 
1) Add deploy-time validation to ensure target pool kernel and GPU memory meets feature flag requirements (e.g., aggressive_batching requires >=40GB and kernel >=1.1).
2) Make "aggressive_batching" default false for canary rollouts; require manual opt-in and presubmit check.
3) Add a canary-target sanity check that flags mixed-capability pools.
4) Postmortem + customer comms.

kevin_sre: I'll own #1 and #3, aim to ship guardrails by EOD tomorrow. @maya_eng please include regression test in runtime CI for batch_size > 8 on lower-memory images.

maya_eng: Will add test and a small perf gate.

jamie_oncall: Good catch everyone. Closing incident when postmortem is posted and customer notified. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Incident closure triggered pending postmortem link.
